item.title: Has Vivek Ramaswamy’s attack ad against Amy Acton backfired?
item.description:
Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is closing out one of the nastiest races of the 2026 cycle by suggesting that Democrat Dr. Amy Acton, his opponent in the Ohio governor’s race, has lied about the well-documented childhood sexual abuse she experienced for political gain. In a contest already marked by sharp personal attacks and partisan rancor, Ramaswamy’s latest attempt to paint Acton as unfit for office came in the form of a minute-long ad this week featuring Donna Arthur, Acton’s estranged mother. item.title: Bodycam video shows police shooting death of one-year-old Kohen Wiley – deconstructed
item.description:
After the Mississippi attorney general cleared a white cop for firing into a car and killing a Black toddler in a Walmart parking lot, video footage released by the Mississippi Department of Public Safety has revealed the fullest picture to date of what happened. The videos, provided to The Intercept in response to a public records request, come on the heels of leaked footage that exposed how a needlessly aggressive and reckless police confrontation of two suspected shoplifters led to 1-year-old Kohen Wiley’s violent death in his mother’s arms. item.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders unionize after years of fighting for fair pay
item.description:
After years of fighting for better pay and benefits, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have unionized. The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association announced Friday that the team has voluntarily recognized the cheerleaders as a collective bargaining unit following a “meaningful discussion.” That gives the newly formed union a green light to begin negotiating. If successful, they would be the first NFL cheer squad to reach a contract. It’s another win for football’s biggest cheerleading brand, which last year secured a 400 percent raise coming off the massive success of “America’s Sweethearts,” the Netflix documentary series that put on full display the athleticism and talent it takes to be a competitive NFL cheerleader — and what little pay comes with the job. The cheerleaders have for years worked together behind the scenes — at one point threatening to stage a walkout — to win higher…

item.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
item.description:
On this day in 1973, Richard Nixon agreed to turn over White House tapes to Judge John Sirica – a key step on the road to the threat of impeachment and removal that persuaded a Republican president to resign in disgrace. Happy Friday… Swin here. We’re in the closing days of the extraordinarily high-stakes 2026 midterms, and if Donald Trump and the Republican Party lose control of the U.S. House and Senate in an electoral “ bloodbath ,” they will largely have Trump and his illegal war on Iran to thank . So what does our genius president do next? He’s busy preparing to make the Iran war somehow even shittier and more painful for us all.
